body.x: Nikon showcased its “SnapBridge”, a wireless connection application for smart devices that can connect digital cameras and smart devices wirelessly via Bluetooth low energy (hereafter BLE), at “CES (Consumer Electronic Show) 2016”, the world’s largest IT electronics and tech exhibition, which runs for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

Minimizing electricity consumption by using BLE, SnapBridge can also connect wirelessly digital cameras and smart devices, and transmit images and data immediately. Starting with its flagship DX-format DSLR camera D500, the company will use SnapBridge for all of its cameras to be launched after 2016.
Nikon will introduce the upgraded convenience of its digital cameras, as well as its strengthened software through this presentation on its applications.
SnapBridge is efficient when people use SNS, such as blogs, Instagram, and Facebook. It is the same with cloud service, as it can be directly connected and transmit data without additional cables.

Furthermore, by connecting cameras to smart devices, it can automatically apply to cameras photo information, including the date, time, and location. It can connect a camera to up to five smart devices by using the pairing setting.

It can also automatically transmit and preserve high-quality original images like JPEG files and 2-megapixel images, even when users are shooting them. With its remote control function, it can check in real time and easily control objects.

The SnapBridge application was launched on iOS and Android versions, and can be downloaded on Apple’s App Store and Google Play for free. It has not yet been decided when the company will start providing the service.
Nikon Imaging Korea CEO Yamada Koichiro said: “Nikon’s SnapBridge is an entirely different, new technology. It will provide users with the utmost convenience that they have never experienced.”

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), CES 2016 is the world's largest exhibition to see the latest global trends in electronics and IT industry in one spot.

AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES for 11 years to introduce the new technologies and products. After the local coverage and research, AVING News will hold 'CES 2016 Review Conference' in AVING Studio, Korea on January 28th.
